item.title: The case for AI degrowth
item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02617-y

Artificial intelligence (AI), as it currently unfolds, is incompatible with a sustainable transformation of the economy, which arguably requires degrowth. AI is the growth paradigm reborn — built on enclosed commons, powered by fossil energy, and driven by a competitive logic that makes precaution structurally impossible. Limits to AI growth are not technophobia; they are our best chance for a liveable future for all.
item.dc:title: The case for AI degrowth
item.dc:creator: Matthias Schmelzer

item.title: Motor abstraction training generalizes to the refinement of specific movement patterns
item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02597-z

Practicing unfamiliar characters in rotated orientations improved upright writing as much as direct practice, showing that the motor system learns by abstracting a movement’s structure, not just its details.
item.dc:title: Motor abstraction training generalizes to the refinement of specific movement patterns
item.dc:creator: Zekun Sun
Zhiran Xie
Samuel D. McDougle

item.content:encoded:
